title: Rabbi Chanina Torteya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:5: “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha in the name of Rabbi Chiyya bar Va: Rabbi Chanina Tarteya ruled in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.” In Jerusalem Talmud Peah 3:7: “Rabbi Yonah, Rabbi Chanina Torteya in the name of Chizkiyah: It is written, ‘And their father gave them gifts.’” In Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:5 the statement is cited in the name of Rabbi Chananyah Tarteya. At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Terumot, chapter 7: Rabbi Chanina Torteyah in the name of Rabbi Yannai, concerning an onion of terumah that was uprooted; the statement is cited in Nedarim 57b in the name of “Rabbi Chanina Teritaah, who said that Rabbi Yannai said,” and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha resolved [the question] for Yishmael of Kefar Yama from it. In Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 10:6: Rabbi Chanina Tirta in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya: “bulb vegetables with bulb vegetables — a kind in its own kind.” In Menachot 48a: “Rabbi Chanina Terita recited a baraita” (Dikdukei Soferim: Tirta). In Temurah 29a and 31a: “Rabbi Chanina Teritaah recited a baraita before Rabbi Yochanan.” In Keritot 9a he asked Rabbi Yochanan. Seder HaDorot, under the entry Rabbi Chanina ben Toreta, cites a story about him, how he was a gentile and converted through his animal; this story is cited in Pesikta Rabbati, piska Parah, under the name of Rabbi Yochanan ben Toreta.

notes.text: Saved Guggenheimer Berakhot3:5 fully writes Shimon ben Elazar, not ben Abba. Saved Guggenheimer English Terumot10:6 calls חסית bulb vegetables, not lettuce. All Torteya/Tarteya/Tirta/Teritaah variants and the Chanina/Yochanan ben Toreta story contrast remain; reciting a baraita is not an automatic Tannaitic-era assignment.

Guggenheimer Berakhot 3:5 directly writes Shimon ben Elazar, and Guggenheimer’s English Terumot 10:6 gives bulb vegetables. These support the retained corrections without collapsing the Torteya/Tarteya/Tirta/Teritaah forms or Chanina into Yochanan ben Toreta. The exact Dikdukei Soferim and Seder HaDorot editions were not inspected; a reciter occurrence is not an automatic tannaitic-era assignment.
